processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
After homogenization the ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm, then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples by electrical discharge machining.
Samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching (as-solution-treated baseline hardness of the 19Al alloy = 263.8 ± 1.1 HV).
The solution-treated sample was aged at 625 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching (this is the terminal state defining the current sample).

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 625 °C for 1 h the α (BCC) matrix of the 19Al alloy had almost completely transformed into β-Mn, with numerous fine BCC and FCC (Cu-rich) precipitates distributed within the β-Mn. The as-solution-treated starting structure was single-phase α (BCC).

phases_present.morphology: matrix formed by nearly complete α→β-Mn transformation
fine precipitates within β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: Fine FCC Cu-rich (with FCC twins) and BCC particles form at the β-Mn interfaces; the BCC phase is attributed to enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces, while the Cu-rich phase arises from the limited solubility of Cu and its expulsion from the growing β-Mn.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average of 5 measurements reported.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times, hardness given as the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the aged 19Al sample
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al aged at 625 °C for 1 h has a Vickers hardness of 855.6 ± 20.8 HV (Table 4); as-solution-treated baseline of the 19Al alloy is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished samples; 50 µm main field with a 10 µm inset for the 19Al 625 °C-1 h panel
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the precipitate morphology/second-phase distribution of the aged 19Al alloy
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 19Al alloy aged at 625 °C for 1 h shows a low-contrast, largely transformed matrix (β-Mn) with only faint fine detail in the 10 µm inset, consistent with near-complete α→β-Mn transformation at ≥600 °C after 1 h.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM with EDS detector
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the chemical composition of the studied alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al alloy composition (at.%): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (Table 1).

unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high (>900 HV) hardness was mainly 575–625 °C, shifted upward relative to 15Al and 17Al, reflecting the slowed β-Mn precipitation kinetics with increasing Al content.
At temperatures of 600 °C and above, the α matrix of the 19Al alloy had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h of aging, with numerous fine BCC and FCC precipitates within the β-Mn.
The 19Al alloy has the highest Al content of the studied series (19Al, Fe 41.6 / Mn 34.8 / Al 18.6 / Cu 5.0 at.%) and its solution-treated state is single-phase α (BCC).

Hardness of the 19Al alloy at 625 °C increased only slightly with aging time (855.6 ± 20.8 HV at 1 h, 863.9 ± 15.8 HV at 3 h, 870.7 ± 16.1 HV at 6 h, 869.5 ± 8.6 HV at 10 h), i.e. the 625 °C hardness is essentially time-independent.
